name: Ahiezer
overview: Ahiezer was a male leader from the tribe of Benjamin, recognized as a chief among the Benjamites. He is noted for coming to David at Ziklag, demonstrating his allegiance during a pivotal moment in Israel's history. His role highlights the support David received from various tribal leaders as he consolidated his kingdom.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahiezer means '[my] brother is a help,' reflecting a sense of supportive kinship. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 12:3, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful Hebrew significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Ahiezer was the father of Shemaah, establishing a direct familial link. Beyond this, there are no additional family relationships noted in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ahiezer's significance lies in his leadership as a chief of the Benjamites who aligned with David at Ziklag. This alliance was crucial in uniting the tribes under David's leadership and securing his reign. His inclusion among those who came to David signifies the broad support David garnered from key tribal figures during a formative period.
